# Review — odyssey-110 (22.398–501), passes 1 and 2

## Source punctuation (for the coordinator; `t` not touched)
- 22.430, after Ὀδυσσεύς: the line ends with no mark in the pinned source (`τὴν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς`), while the same formula at 22.490 and in odyssey-024 has `·`. A speech follows, so Murray surely prints a stop; this looks like rule 5. Adding `·` would not change the unit cut (unit 19 is already one line) and would make the whole unit identical in `t` to odyssey-024's. The draft's note had claimed "Murray prints no punctuation"; that claim is removed (see table), so nothing else depends on it.
- 22.497 ends `ἔχουσαι.` with a full stop (the same formula has a comma at 4.300 in odyssey-016). The source is followed; the unit is cut there (see table).
- All other lines without end punctuation (440, 468) are mid-sentence cuts at a comma in sentences longer than four lines, and are right.

## Checked and found right
- `t` rebuilds the packet exactly (as words); `ln` correct on every unit including the four new ones; `l` and `t` have the same number of lines in all 61 units; no `\n` in `i`.
- `p` on all 13 ¶ lines (398, 411, 419, 430, 433, 437, 446, 462, 465, 474, 478, 490, 492) and nowhere else.
- `mark` on the first unit of all 8 speeches (411, 420, 431, 437, 462, 481, 486, 491); “ on first unit and ” on last unit of every speech in both `l` and `i`, none open at end of part. The part opens after odyssey-109's closed ” (Telemachus's call at 22.395–397): no speech runs in; none runs out.
- Published repeats identical in `l`/`i`: 22.398, 22.410, 22.414–415, 22.416, 22.419, 22.420, 22.430, 22.433–434, 22.485, 22.490, 22.496, 22.497, 22.499. 22.409 matches odyssey-016/081 (ἱεμένω/ἱεμένους) with the feminine singular correctly adapted.
- Table renderings followed: ἄπτερος μῦθος, ὁσίη (holy/right), σχέτλια ἔργα, κατὰ μοῖραν (3.331), περικαλλής, ἐϋσταθής, ἀμύμων, κυανόπρῳρος, νηλεής, κεκοτηότι θυμῷ, γρηῦς, ἄσπετον, θαλερὸν δάκρυ, αἴθουσα, πρόθυρον "forecourt", σιγαλόεις/ὑπερώϊα, ἀτιμάζουσι, ἑξείης, ἀνάγκη "under compulsion", ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα, φίλη τροφός.
- Cross-references checked: 395–397 (odyssey-109), 402, 427, 430, 434, 438–439, 441–442, 448, 458–459.
- Scansion flags: none in the packet; nothing to add.

## Considered and refused
- Unit 37 `i` "the lives" against `l` "the life" for θυμόν: plural reads naturally for the many women; the note says "the life".
- Unit 43 `i` "hearts full of resentment" against the table's "a heart full of resentment": the plural follows the plural subject, as the table does for person; left.
- Unit 28 note "terribly" for αἰνά: it glosses the Greek, the `l`/`i` ("fearsomely", "bitterly") follow new-renderings; left.
- Unit 12 `l` "list" for κατάλεξον: the glossary has "recount in full and in order"; "list" is fine for the sense and matches the note.
- Unit 15 `i` "to do their work" for ἔργα ἐργάζεσθαι: `l` keeps the figure.
- Unit 2 `i` word order "She found Odysseus then": natural English; `l` keeps the Greek order.
- Unit 5 `i` drops οὖν: `l` has "then".
- Unit 41 `i` "though not for long at all": περ concessive, fine.
- Unit 58 (500) `i` "knew them all" for γίγνωσκε: the note glosses "recognise"; "knew" is the sense in context.
- Unit 26 ἀμύμων "blameless" of a fence: kept every time by the table; the note says so.
- Unit 38 note "The pillar is not otherwise described in this part": empty but true; left.
- αἰνύμεναι (500) is accented like an infinitive but is read as a participle ("taking hold"), as the sense demands; glosser's parse kept.
